title: Report Comparison: Hazira gas release and fire, 2020
status: Learning purposes: not a statutory document. Derived from a ProbeMatrix investigation export; learnings are evidence-linked but should be validated by the organisation before adoption.

data_quality.text: Draft learnings from an unreviewed analysis: the export's Investigation Status is in progress and no finding is marked as edited by a person.

bottom_line.text: Same evidence, different analytical architecture: the export was built from the enquiry committee's own report, so this compares how far each analysis takes the same facts, not the quality of either investigation.

Coverage is close both ways: every one of the 25 register learnings has a counterpart in the committee's report (21 at the same level, 4 in part), and 76 of its 84 items map to a learning (46 fully, 30 in part).

What the second look adds is the organisational reason behind four conditions: no independent check on a high-consequence repair (LR-03), repeat seal failures not read as a warning (LR-05), a response that stayed on finding the leak (LR-08), and warnings softened as they were relayed (LR-13).

Control strength differs: 25 of the committee's 35 recommendations are administrative and 8 engineering; the register's 44 recommendations hold 20 engineering and 4 elimination or substitution changes.

The committee is stronger on plant-specific engineering and testing detail, such as the fire-pump test regime, incident classification, logbooks and control-room layout, which the export does not code as conditions of their own.

items.text: Comparison against the other report: Enquiry committee report on the major fire at the Hazira gas processing plant on 24.09.2020 (enquiry committee constituted by the national petroleum and natural gas regulator; regulator-constituted enquiry under an office order of 30.09.2020; the report does not name the statutory provision). The comparison covers analysis coverage, not the quality of either investigation.

Sighted comparison. The evidence behind the export is the committee's report itself: 8 of the 46 evidence items quote or point to its recommendations, and 92 of the 436 findings refer to them in their reasoning. This is report coverage, not independent discovery. The committee had site access, eyewitness interviews, CCTV and control-room records; the export re-analyses the committee's account of them through the four HFACS levels.

Conflict of interest: this comparison was written with the ProbeMatrix learnings coach, so one of the two compared analyses is the toolmaker's own. Read the counts with that in mind, and review the match judgments in comparison-map.json before relying on them. The operator is not a compared party.

sections.heading: Where the other report is stronger

items.text: The committee's fire-fighting section is more specific than the export: pump run frequency and capacity tests against the industry standard, diesel logs, maintenance split across departments, and the reporting line of the fire crews (OBS-15 to OBS-20, REC-11 to REC-16). The export codes the unavailable diesel pumps (LR-23) but not the test regime [FND-A4B843EB; EVD-2432].

It also covers topics the export does not code as conditions of their own: incident classification and review (OBS-11, REC-07), logbooks and handover records (OBS-43, REC-35), control-room panel layout (REC-31) and storage of rubber spares (REC-27). They come from the committee's own review of records it was given [EVD-3452].

Its evidence is first-hand: the site inspection, eyewitness interviews, CCTV frames and control-room data. Several recommendations are direct plant changes the operator can act on, such as unique tags on every flameproof fitting (REC-24) and remote operation of all motor-operated valves (REC-03) [FND-ABF11182; EVD-0496; FND-02310148; EVD-3932].

Desk analysis: the export saw only what the committee wrote. It could not see the plant, the people or the records, and its findings inherit the committee's facts and any gaps in them. The committee's report gives two different years for one seal change, and the export follows the later one [FND-82FC718D; EVD-1494].

Transcription: the comparator inventory was typed by hand from the text layer of the report PDF, with roles in place of names and functions in place of company names. Recommendations were split by their sub-numbers (A.1 into its drawing and control-system parts; B.5, C.1, C.2 and D.1 to D.3 by sub-item). The control tiers of the committee's recommendations are this comparison's classification, not the committee's.

Two findings quote recommendation text, numbered D.2.iii and D.2.iv, that the committee's report does not contain [FND-7A32AC87; FND-212DC9B7]; the comparison uses the report's own wording. Counts here are learnings and comparator items, not finding instances.
